concerns.text: Tasks T060–T064 implement a 'Human Judgment Simulation' (System 1/2 bias modeling) that has no corresponding Functional Requirement, User Story, or Success Criterion in spec.md or plan.md. This constitutes scope creep and violates the constraint that tasks must strictly satisfy authorized requirements (FR-001 to FR-006, US-01 to US-03).

Task T027 embeds a non-executable pseudo-code formula string ('The memory footprint will be estimated based on...') directly into the implementation logic description. This weakens the deterministic requirement for executable, verifiable code logic (FR-006) by introducing ambiguous, prose-based instructions that cannot be directly translated into code without interpretation.

Task T004 defines `ALPHA_LEVELS = [, 0.05, 0.10]` with a leading comma and missing first value. This is a syntax error that prevents the task from satisfying FR-005 (configuration of significance thresholds) and creates a broken baseline for downstream tasks (T023, T033).

Task T022 asserts it verifies SC-004 (3 alpha levels) but depends on T022b (CLI validation logic) which is marked as unstarted (`[ ]`). This creates a logical gap where the verification step (T022) cannot functionally satisfy the success criterion (SC-004) because the prerequisite enforcement logic (T022b) is missing.

Task T023 defines `ALPHA_LEVELS` defaults as `[0.01, 0.05, 0.10]` in the description, but T004 (which it depends on) has a syntax error in the same constant. This semantic inconsistency weakens the requirement for a consistent configuration baseline required by FR-005.
